extracted.intended_audience: Public Information Officers, incident communicators, and agency staff involved in incident report rollouts (BIA and wildland fire agencies)
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and executing an incident communications strategy and rollout (press release, briefings, web posting, personal briefings) for a wildfire/burnover investigation report, including audience segmentation, key messages, action items, and media relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication Goal (timely release)
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of this communications plan is to release the findings of the Sawtooth Mountain Accident Investigation Team's report concerning the firefighter burnover and subsequent fatality in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize timeliness when scheduling and executing all rollout activities; align all tasks and approvals to meet the release window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform primary and other audiences of report progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform the primary and other audiences progress of report release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide regular status updates to both primary (family, on-site participants, BIA/tribal employees) and secondary audiences through appropriate channels until the report is released.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a timeline for report release
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a time line for report release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce a schedule that includes milestones, approval points, and final release date/time; integrate with action plan and assign owners and due-dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate timeline into an action plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate the time line into a 'mini' action plan for report release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate timeline into discrete action items (who/what/by when) such as briefings, materials production, and web posting; track completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate release of the Accident Investigation Report
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate the release of the Accident Investigation Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure interagency coordination (NIFC, regional offices), approvals, and unified messaging prior to release; confirm distribution channels are ready.

rubrics_metrics.name: List participants and define roles & responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a list of participants and their roles and responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For every action item and audience contact, assign a named person responsible (Who) and a backup; include contact information and escalation path.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify resource needs for release
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify other resource needs for release of the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for materials production (CD-ROMs, print copies), travel, staffing for briefings/interviews, technical support for web posting, and media staging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience identification and segmentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Break down audiences as local/internal (directly involved or affected), external/regional/national (not directly involved), and political.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly list primary audiences (family, on-site personnel, BIA/tribal members) and map each to appropriate communication methods and timing (e.g., personal briefings before public release).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority for primary/local audiences (personal briefings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary audiences for personal meetings include the Lupe family and those involved in the incident; members of the team and others will meet personally with family members, employees, and tribal leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule and conduct face-to-face or phone briefings with primary audiences prior to public dissemination; provide full report and Q&A materials in person where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key messages (clear, consistent themes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop key messages such as: the team is fact-finding not fault-finding; firefighter/public safety is top priority; team members were selected for qualifications and followed prescribed investigation guidance; the team was professional and objective; the team established probable events and documented findings to prevent future occurrences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft concise, audience-tailored key messages and ensure all speakers and materials use the same language; include message hierarchy for difficult questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select appropriate communication methods per audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a mix of personal meetings, media, press briefings/conferences, agency internet sites (NIFC), face-to-face meetings, email, and CD-ROM distribution to reach different audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match method to audience (e.g., personal briefing for family; web posting and press conference for public); have alternate delivery methods for those without web access (CD-ROM, mailed copies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Action plan table: specify what/who/when for each audience
rubrics_metrics.description: For each target audience document Communication Method, What (material), Who (responsible), and timing (By When or date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a delivery matrix that assigns content (report, CD-ROM, web link), responsible individuals, and dates; include contingency steps if personnel are unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed rollout action checklist with owners & deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an Action Plan for Report Rollout listing items (e.g., request investigation bios, send rollout plan for review, confirm meetings, develop materials list, order copies, set up briefings, identify spokesperson, finalize Q&As/fact sheets, finalize travel, issue press release) with assigned owners and dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track all rollout tasks, mark completed items, and follow through on procurement and logistics (e.g., order 100 CD-ROMs, quick-copy report orders).

rubrics_metrics.name: Press conference structure and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Rollout press conference/briefing should not last more than 60 minutes; maximum of 45 minutes allowed after the conference for one-on-one interviews; maximum of two speakers on the podium plus the facilitator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere strictly to time limits; plan sequence (intro, director remarks, investigation process, timeline of events, findings, Q&A) and enforce Q&A time caps (e.g., 15 minutes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dry-run and 'mini-murder board' preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: The presentation team should complete a dry-run on-site prior to the rollout and conduct a 'mini-murder board' (crisis communications training to practice hostile interview questions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rehearse presentations, rehearse responses to tough questions, prepare props (e.g., two enlarged photos), and ensure technical and logistical issues are resolved before the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designate spokesperson(s) and technical backup
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify a Spokesperson for any post-release inquiries; have a technical person with the director at all times during interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announce designated spokesperson(s) in materials; ensure backup is briefed and available for one-on-one interviews and technical clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synchronize multi-channel release timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate simultaneous activities such as issuing the press release, flipping the news release switch, posting information on the web, courtesy emails, and phone briefings at the same scheduled time (examples show 1400).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate exact timing to all participants (who will 'flip the switch'); prepare web hosting and distribution lists in advance to enable near-instant publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop Q&As and fact sheets for sensitive topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalize backgrounds, Q and A's, Fact Sheets (e.g., fire shelter talking points, deployment, equipment implementation timelines, cause of death, compensation) to address likely media and public questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate sensitive or technical questions (compensation, safety, equipment transition) and prepare clear, factual answers; include references to policy or manuals where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor social media and project future information demands
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor social media to determine information that may need to be addressed or clarified through media messaging and project public/media demands for the next hours and days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use social monitoring to identify rumors or misinformation; plan follow-up messaging and schedule updates accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand media needs and deadlines; use a media log
rubrics_metrics.description: Each media outlet has specific deadlines; use a media log and identify each media representative’s deadlines in their first entry or ask for their deadline and meet it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record reporters' contact info and deadlines; prioritize information delivery to meet those deadlines; prepare short-form and long-form materials as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor messaging to media type and scope of coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Local media want specific details; regional/national want the big picture. National/regional may require agency approval; they may be aggressive and expect access and mobile technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust depth and focus of information based on outlet type; notify agency officials when national coverage is anticipated; be tactful and stress safety when dealing with aggressive reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire services should be contacted first for significant incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Wire services should be the first media outlet you contact when an incident with any significant potential occurs; they usually want a large amount of detailed information and may want site visits or sidebars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare detailed incident summaries, graphics, and availability for follow-up; anticipate wire dissemination leading to broader national/regional pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medium-specific delivery: newspapers, radio, television guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Newspapers want detailed information and graphics; radio requires frequent, concise updates and may tape interviews by phone; television prioritizes pictures and human emotion and often wants access to the scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide newspapers with detailed facts and photos; for radio prepare short soundbites and frequent updates; for television prepare visuals, B-roll, and on-camera spokespeople; treat photographers equitably and coordinate photo locations with operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain comprehensive contact and legislative/political lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep contact information for team members, media outlets (including Native American outlets), and legislative/political contacts (governor, congressional offices) for courtesy calls and targeted briefings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compile phone, cell, fax, and email for all relevant contacts; plan courtesy calls or briefings for political offices and provide roll-out updates as requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and protocols for Q&A and interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Set protocols for Q&A (e.g., Palmrose to facilitate Questions and Answers; maximum 15 minutes regardless) and one-on-one interviews (max 45 minutes post-conference, have technical person present, end interviews on schedule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce ground rules publicly (time limits, facilitator control); structure who answers technical vs policy questions and manage follow-up commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize investigation scope and methodology in messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: State that the Accident Investigation Team is a fact-finding team, not a fault-finding team, and that investigations were conducted according to Departmental Manual 485 Chapter 7 and USDA-Forest Service 'Investigating Wildland Fire Entrapments' guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite methodology and standards to bolster credibility; reference authoritative documents when describing investigative approach.
